legend: For her social studies project, Cindy is doing extensive research into the Three Kingdoms period of Chinese History. Her primary sources are works of media centered on legendary Shu tactician Zhuge Liang (courtesy name Kongming)—these range from speculative fiction of how a strategist of Kongming's caliber would fare in cutthroat industries of the modern day, as well as rigorous combat simulations that highlight Zhuge Liang's own personal combat prowess and ability to decimate hundreds of enemies en masse using magic.
Through her research, she encountered this quite interesting excerpt:

I asked my army to divide themselves into squadrons such that each squadron contained the same number of soldiers. I know that they will do this task to the best of their ability, forming as many groups of that size as possible, as much as possible. However, depending on the squadron size I choose, it may be possible that despite their efforts, there may be soldiers left over who are unable to form a complete squadron.
I asked them to divide themselves into squadrons of size a1$$$a_1$$$, but this unfortunately resulted in k$$$k$$$ people left over.
I asked them to divide themselves into squadrons of size a2$$$a_2$$$, but this unfortunately resulted in k$$$k$$$ people left over.
I asked them to divide themselves into squadrons of size a3$$$a_3$$$, but this unfortunately resulted in k$$$k$$$ people left over.

...and so on. I did this n$$$n$$$ times—asking them to form as many squadrons as possible of sizes a1$$$a_1$$$, then a2$$$a_2$$$, ..., then an$$$a_n$$$—but every single time, there were exactly k$$$k$$$ people left over and unable to form a complete squadron. What a coincidence!

Cindy found, through another source, that the number of soldiers in Zhuge Liang's army was between ℓ$$$\ell$$$ and r$$$r$$$, inclusive. Given this information, how many soldiers were in Zhuge Liang's army?
If there are multiple possible answers, output any of them. If there are no possible answers (meaning the historical sources are inaccurate), you must say so as well.
input: The first line of input contains the space-separated integers n$$$n$$$, ℓ$$$\ell$$$, r$$$r$$$, and k$$$k$$$.
The second line of input contains the n$$$n$$$ distinct space-separated integers a1,a2,…,an$$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$$.
output: If an answer exists, output any integer x$$$x$$$ such that ℓ≤x≤r$$$\ell \leq x \leq r$$$, and x$$$x$$$ soldiers would result in the described scenario. If there are multiple possible answers, output any of them.
If there are no possible answers, output −1$$$-1$$$ instead.

legend.ai: Cindy 正在为她的社会学科项目，对中国历史上的三国时期进行广泛研究。她的主要资料来源是以传奇般的蜀国军师诸葛亮（字孔明）为中心的媒体作品，其范围从推测一位孔明级别的谋士在现代激烈竞争的行业中将如何表现的科幻作品，到突出诸葛亮个人战斗能力，以及他使用魔法一次性大量歼灭数百名敌人的严谨战斗模拟。
通过她的研究，她遇到了下面这段颇为有趣的摘录：
我要求我的军队将自己分成若干小队，使得每个小队包含相同数量的士兵。我知道，他们会尽其所能完成这项任务，尽可能多地组成这么多人的小队。然而，根据我选择的小队人数，即使他们已经尽力，仍可能有一些士兵无法组成一个完整的小队而剩下。
我要求他们组成每队人数为 a1$$$a_1$$$ 的小队，但遗憾的是，这导致有 k$$$k$$$ 人剩下。
我要求他们组成每队人数为 a2$$$a_2$$$ 的小队，但遗憾的是，这导致有 k$$$k$$$ 人剩下。
我要求他们组成每队人数为 a3$$$a_3$$$ 的小队，但遗憾的是，这导致有 k$$$k$$$ 人剩下。
……以此类推。我一共进行了 n$$$n$$$ 次操作，要求他们依次尽可能多地组成每队人数为 a1$$$a_1$$$、然后为 a2$$$a_2$$$、……、最后为 an$$$a_n$$$ 的小队，但每一次都恰好有 k$$$k$$$ 人剩下，无法组成一个完整的小队。真是巧合！
Cindy 通过另一个来源得知，诸葛亮的军队人数在 ℓ$$$\ell$$$ 和 r$$$r$$$ 之间(包含两端)。根据这一信息，诸葛亮的军队中有多少名士兵？
如果有多个可能的答案，输出其中任意一个。如果不存在可能的答案（即历史资料不准确），也必须说明这一点。

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含用空格分隔的整数 n$$$n$$$、ℓ$$$\ell$$$、r$$$r$$$ 和 k$$$k$$$。
输入的第二行包含 n$$$n$$$ 个互不相同的、用空格分隔的整数 a1,a2,…,an$$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$$。

如果不存在可能的答案，则输出 −1$$$-1$$$。
